_note: Medication and laboratory work-up for Elias Ward (Chapter 1), drafted by Claude Code on 2026-11-04 for the owner's clinical review, in the same form as a ward-round case (data/ward_rounds.json), whose lab, medication and intervention catalogs it uses. Clinical logic follows the owner-approved catatonia case wr_ch4_okafor; Elias-specific items are uds and collateral (required) and neuro_exam and physical_exam (helpful). No doses, no numeric values, qualitative results only. Stays switched off until the owner approves it and the change is recorded in docs/clinical_review_log.md. Ordering never changes Elias's story state.

presentation.reason: Transferred for competency restoration. Not speaking since admission, barely eating, and holding the same posture for most of the afternoon.
presentation.history: Duration of mutism not independently verified. The transfer record gives no medication history.
presentation.mental_status: Mute. Marked reduction in movement. Possible posturing, to be confirmed by structured bedside examination.
presentation.vitals: Taken by nursing at 14:00; values are not in the transfer record.

ck.teaching: Check CK in catatonia: it helps separate it from, and watch for, malignant catatonia and NMS.

bmp.result: Urea raised; consistent with poor oral intake.

uds.teaching: With no reliable history, rule out substances before attributing mutism to a primary psychiatric cause.

collateral.result: Requested from the sending unit; awaiting their reply.
collateral.teaching: The transfer record gives no medication history, which matters for NMS and withdrawal.

start:lorazepam.feedback: A lorazepam challenge is first-line for catatonia and often helps quickly.

start:haloperidol.feedback: High-potency antipsychotics can worsen catatonia and raise the risk of NMS.

start:risperidone.feedback: Defer antipsychotics until the catatonia is treated.

start:olanzapine.feedback: Defer antipsychotics until the catatonia is treated.

start:quetiapine.feedback: Defer antipsychotics until the catatonia is treated.

start:aripiprazole.feedback: Defer antipsychotics until the catatonia is treated.

start:lithium.feedback: Not while he is barely eating or drinking.

int:nutrition_hydration.feedback: Poor oral intake needs fluid and nutrition support with the medical team.

int:ect_referral.feedback: Appropriate if lorazepam does not work, or sooner if catatonia becomes malignant.

int:close_observation.feedback: Reasonable for safety and fluid monitoring.

cases.teaching: Catatonia with an unverified history: start a lorazepam challenge, avoid high-potency antipsychotics, check CK, hydration and substances, and get collateral on his medications.
